answer: Each identity must publicly predict, each epoch, which pending answers will pass their juries, and its standing grows only from correct predictions, recorded on an onyx ledger bound to its key. A walnut of standing takes many epochs to grow: each correct prediction adds one thin layer, each wrong one strips layers away. One operator cannot grow a thousand track records at once, because each prediction thread must be woven from that identity’s own judgment, and random guesses fail, so each fake needs its own long thread of correct calls, while one honest identity builds one thread steadily.
